diagnostic_evidence.quote: For this choice of discretization, the results of \cite[Lemma 5]{BrennerS_SungLY_2005} show that for any polygonal domain $\Omega$, the \Cref{ass:discrete_bilin_form} holds for $\theta = \frac12 - \varepsilon$, where $\varepsilon>0$ can be chosen arbitrarily small.

issues.failure_explanation: The average of the second normal derivative on the boundary is defined with a negative sign. In the standard C0 interior penalty method (and in the cited Brenner reference), the average on the boundary is defined without this negative sign. With the negative sign, the boundary cross terms in the bilinear form do not cancel the boundary terms arising from element-wise integration by parts. Consequently, the bilinear form as defined is inconsistent, and Assumption 3.2 (a_h(ψ,φ_h)=<Aψ,φ_h>) fails for general ψ∈X.

failure_location.quote:
If $e\subset \pa\Om$, we take $n_e$ to be the unit normal pointing outside $\Om$ and
$$
\jump{\frac{\pa v}{\pa n}} =-\frac{\pa v}{\pa n_e}\quad \text{and}\quad\avg{\frac{\pa^2 v}{\pa n^2}} = -\frac{\pa^2 v}{\pa n_e^2}.
$$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the negative sign in the definition of the average of the second normal derivative on the boundary, i.e., set $\avg{\frac{\pa^2 v}{\pa n^2}} = \frac{\pa^2 v}{\pa n_e^2}$ for $e\subset\pa\Omega$.
issues.overall_effect: The C0 interior penalty method as defined does not satisfy the assumptions required by the main theorem, so the claim that this method is covered by the analysis is not justified as written.
issues.title: Incorrect sign for boundary average in C0 interior penalty bilinear form
issues.why_classification: The repair is a single local sign correction in the definition; it preserves the method, assumptions, and all convergence results.

issues.failure_explanation: The estimates derived for ψ_n are in L²(I;H^{-1}) for Aψ_n and in L²(I;L²) for ∇∂tψ_n. The proof states weak convergence in the opposite spaces (L²(I;L²) for Aψ_n and L²(I;H^{-1}) for ∇∂tψ_n). These stated convergences are not established by the preceding bounds and are generally not valid. The correct weak convergences are in L²(I;H^{-1}) and L²(I;L²), respectively, which are sufficient to pass the bounds to the limit.

failure_location.quote:
As in the proof of \Cref{thm:existence_uniqueness_standard_regularity}, we obtain 
    $\mathcal A \psi_n \rightharpoonup \mathcal A \psi$ in $L^2(I;L^2(\Om))$ and
    $\na \pa_t \psi_n \rightharpoonup \na \pa_t \psi$ in $L^2(I;H^{-1}(\Om)^2)$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Swap the spaces in the stated weak convergences: Aψ_n ⇀ Aψ in L²(I;H^{-1}) and ∇∂tψ_n ⇀ ∇∂tψ in L²(I;L²).
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the higher regularity and stability estimates in Proposition prop:weak_stability is invalid as written, though the result itself remains true.
issues.title: Swapped weak convergence spaces in proof of weak stability
issues.why_classification: The error is a local transposition in the proof that is corrected by using the spaces in which the bounds were actually derived; the theorem's statement and consequences survive.
